{{Short description|Construction for simplicial sets}}
{{Other uses|Twisted diagonal (disambiguation)}}
In [[higher category theory]] in [[mathematics]], the '''twisted diagonal''' of a [[simplicial set]] (for [[∞-category|∞-categories]] also called the '''twisted arrow ∞-category''') is a construction, which generalizes the [[Twisted diagonal (category theory)|twisted diagonal of a category]] to which it corresponds under the [[Nerve (category theory)|nerve]] construction. Since  the twisted diagonal of a category is the [[category of elements]] of the [[Hom functor]], the twisted diagonal of an ∞-category can be used to define the [[Hom functor of an ∞-category]].

== Twisted diagonal with the join operation ==
For a simplicial set <math>A</math> define a [[bisimplicial set]] and a simplicial set with the [[opposite simplicial set]] and the [[Join (simplicial sets)|join of simplicial sets]] by:<ref name=":8">Cisinski 2019, 5.6.1.</ref>

: <math>\mathbf{Tw}(A)_{m,n}
=\operatorname{Hom}((\Delta^m)^\mathrm{op}*\Delta^n,A),</math>
: <math>\operatorname{Tw}(A)
=\delta^*(\mathbf{Tw}(A)).</math>

(<math>\delta^*\colon
\mathbf{bisSet}\rightarrow\mathbf{sSet}</math> is the functor obtained by precomposition with the diagonal <math>\delta\colon\Delta\rightarrow\Delta\times\Delta</math>, hence <math>\delta^*(A)_n=A_{n,n}</math>.) The canonical morphisms <math>(\Delta^m)^\mathrm{op}\rightarrow(\Delta^m)^\mathrm{op}*\Delta^n\leftarrow\Delta^n</math> induce canonical morphisms <math>\mathbf{Tw}(A)\rightarrow A^\mathrm{op}\boxtimes A</math> and <math>\operatorname{Tw}(A)\rightarrow A^\mathrm{op}\times A</math>.<ref name=":8" />

== Twisted diagonal with the diamond operation ==
For a simplicial set <math>A</math> define a bisimplicial set and a simplicial set with the opposite simplicial set and the [[diamond operation]] by:<ref>Cisinski 2019, 5.6.10.</ref>

: <math>\mathbf{Tw}_\diamond(A)_{m,n}
=\operatorname{Hom}((\Delta^m)^\mathrm{op}\diamond\Delta^n,A),</math>
: <math>\operatorname{Tw}_\diamond(A)
=\delta^*(\mathbf{Tw}_\diamond(A)).</math>

The canonical morphisms <math>(\Delta^m)^\mathrm{op}\rightarrow(\Delta^m)^\mathrm{op}\diamond\Delta^n\leftarrow\Delta^n</math> induce canonical morphisms <math>\mathbf{Tw}_\diamond(A)\rightarrow A^\mathrm{op}\boxtimes A</math> and <math>\operatorname{Tw}_\diamond(A)\rightarrow A^\mathrm{op}\times A</math>. The weak categorical equivalence <math>\gamma_{(\Delta^m)^\mathrm{op},\Delta^n}\colon
(\Delta^m)^\mathrm{op}\diamond\Delta^n\rightarrow(\Delta^m)^\mathrm{op}*\Delta^n</math> induces canonical morphisms <math>\mathbf{Tw}(A)\rightarrow\mathbf{Tw}_\diamond(A)</math> and <math>\operatorname{Tw}(A)\rightarrow\operatorname{Tw}_\diamond(A)</math>.

== Properties ==

* Under the [[Nerve (category theory)|nerve]], the twisted diagonal of categories corresponds to the twisted diagonal of simplicial sets. Let <math>\mathcal{C}</math> be a small category, then:<ref name=":16">Kerodon, [https://kerodon.net/tag/03JN Proposition 8.1.1.10.]</ref>
*: <math>N\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal{C})
=\operatorname{Tw}(N\mathcal{C}).</math>
* For an ∞-category <math>A</math>, the canonical map <math>\operatorname{Tw}(A)\rightarrow A^\mathrm{op}\times A</math> is a [[left fibration]]. Therefore, the twisted diagonal <math>\operatorname{Tw}(A)</math> is also an ∞-category.<ref>Cisinski 2019, Proposition 5.6.2.</ref><ref>Kerodon, [https://kerodon.net/tag/03JQ Proposition 8.1.1.11.]</ref><ref>Kerodon, [https://kerodon.net/tag/03JR Corollary 8.1.1.12.]</ref>
* For a Kan complex <math>A</math>, the canonical map <math>\operatorname{Tw}(A)\rightarrow A^\mathrm{op}\times A</math> is a [[Kan fibration]]. Therefore, the twisted diagonal <math>\operatorname{Tw}(A)</math> is also a Kan complex.<ref>Kerodon, [https://kerodon.net/tag/048H Corollary 8.1.1.13.]</ref>
* For an ∞-category <math>A</math>, the canonical map <math>\mathbf{Tw}_\diamond(A)\rightarrow A^\mathrm{op}\boxtimes A</math> is a left bifibration and the canonical map <math>\operatorname{Tw}_\diamond(A)\rightarrow A^\mathrm{op}\times A</math> is a left fibration. Therefore, the simplicial set <math>\operatorname{Tw}_\diamond(A)</math> is also an ∞-category.<ref>Cisinski 2019, Proposition 5.6.12.</ref>
* For an ∞-category <math>A</math>, the canonical morphism <math>\operatorname{Tw}(A)\rightarrow\operatorname{Tw}_\diamond(A)</math> is a fiberwise equivalence of left fibrations over <math>A^\mathrm{op}\times A</math>.<ref>Cisinski 2019, Corollary 5.6.14.</ref>
* A functor <math>u\colon A\rightarrow B</math> between ∞-categories <math>A</math> and <math>B</math> is [[Full and faithful functors|fully faithful]] if and only if the induced map:
*: <math>\operatorname{Tw}(A)\rightarrow(A^\mathrm{op}\times A)\times_{B^\mathrm{op}\times B}\operatorname{Tw}(B)</math>
: is a fiberwise equivalence over <math>A^\mathrm{op}\times A</math>.<ref>Cisinski 2019, Corollary 5.6.6.</ref>
* For a functor <math>u\colon A\rightarrow B</math> between ∞-categories <math>A</math> and <math>B</math>, the induced maps:
*: <math>\operatorname{Tw}(A)\rightarrow(A^\mathrm{op}\times B)\times_{B^\mathrm{op}\times B}\operatorname{Tw}(B),</math>
*: <math>\operatorname{Tw}(A)\rightarrow(B^\mathrm{op}\times A)\times_{B^\mathrm{op}\times B}\operatorname{Tw}(B),</math>
: are cofinal.<ref>Cisinski 2019, Proposition 5.6.9.</ref>
